title: Ripple 65B Preview API Pricing: Price Table for 2026
summary: Ripple 65B Preview API pricing varies across different plans. Compare each option's cost and features to choose the right tier for your needs.
body_markdown:
## Ripple 65B Preview API Pricing Table, Checked Today


### Ripple 65B Preview API pricing in short


Whatever price is listed for Ripple 65B Preview, that is **where your bill starts, not where it ends** .


The final figure depends on the billing unit, the preview limits and the overage rules, and none of the three appears in the headline number, which is why teams that route usage through[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) or any other layer still need to read the fine print first.


Until you know what a unit is, a price quoted per unit tells you nothing. If a preview cap throttles you mid-job, you also learn what the cheap rate was quietly assuming.


> Until you know what a unit is, a price quoted per unit tells you nothing.


The sections after this one show how to turn those three variables into your own monthly figure.


Mind the word "preview": Ripple 65B Preview is a pre-release language model from Ripple, offered through an API under preview terms. Preview terms usually mean limits can change, and sometimes the price can too.


Treat every number on the pricing page as valid for the day you read it, not for the quarter you're budgeting.


### Every plan in one table


To price a workload you need five columns: price and billing unit, inclusions, rate limits and quotas, free allowance, and preview caveats.


Of everything I checked, only Ripple 65B Preview could be confirmed by name, and every one of those five fields for it is "not stated" rather than a guess. Fill any gaps from the vendor's pricing page before you budget.


When every field reads "not stated", that is itself a finding. A preview **with no published limits can throttle you** at a threshold you only discover through an error message.


Read the rest of this article with that in mind, and treat any unstated field as a question to settle before you commit spend.


### How the Ripple 65B pricing was checked


I prepared this page on 16 November 2026. I compared the pricing information available to me against the plan columns above.


I left a field as "not stated" wherever I couldn't confirm it. I didn't infer anything from other vendors' models or from what previews usually look like.


You can recheck cheaply. Open Ripple's pricing page beside this article and fill each unstated field as you find it.


Then log your own usage for a day, and if you build the counter in[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) , a ten-step counter costs the same as a two-step one: 1 credit per flow run, where Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so splitting the work into smaller steps never raises the meter.


A day of real counts will show you which unit Ripple actually bills you in.
